rows.reason: Statement asserts completeness of the sequence norm and then invokes the Hilbert-space definition F3. Proof 1.1 constructs coordinate limits and 2.1 proves norm convergence, without an equivalence classifying other sequence spaces.

The completeness proof ends with every Cauchy sequence converging in the given norm. There is no claim that every Hilbert space is this countable sequence space or a reverse identification of its index set.

Proof 1.1 substitutes the charged redshift identities, then 3.1 computes factorization for independent cells. It does not claim every Gibbs state or interacting reduced state has this tensor factorization.
Neutrality is used in Proof 5.1 to identify the two already defined dynamics. Factorization of a density is not used to recover the charged geometry, stationarity or absence of interactions.

Verification 2.1 directly multiplies Pauli matrices and 3.1 evaluates a re-prepared static family. These establish the displayed qubit formulas without asserting that every oscillatory response comes from this model.

Verification 4.1 excludes a dc relabelling because the supplied sinusoid persists. It never infers a two-level Hamiltonian from a measured spectral pair, and contains no reverse model-classification assertion.

findings.completeness: Proof 1.1 constructs the unique coordinate limit; 2.1 proves convergence in the stated norm and uses the definition of Hilbert space. No inverse classification is asserted.
findings.factorization: Proof 1.1 explicitly retains A2 at charged-stationarity use; 2.1 constructs a product eigenbasis; 3.1 proves the finite tensor density formula, and 4.1–5.1 prove the stated grand and neutral physical KMS properties. None implies that an arbitrary Gibbs state or factorized density determines geometry or independence.
findings.qubit: Verification 1.1–2.2 proves the Pauli weights, response and spectral pushforward, now retaining F2 at the assigned-cell use; 3.1 evaluates the separately prepared static derivative and 4.1 establishes persistence. No inference from observed spectral data to a unique Hamiltonian or preparation is claimed.
